newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat slips further, barley steady.
newsitem.headline: French wheat slips further, barley steady.

text.p: Wheat prices slipped further on Monday on a lack of fresh export demand while barley prices remained steady, dealers said.
Wheat into Rouen was down five francs to 880 francs a tonne for October-November delivery.
Rouen barley fetched 860-870 francs for October-December delivery, unchanged on Friday.

Barley and wheat prices fell last Friday after the European Union failed to grant traders' demands to export large tonnages of free market grain with substantial subsidies. The EU awarded only modest tonnages of grain through its weekly grain tenders.
MATIF wheat futures were at a standstill, with no trade reported by mid-afternoon. Volume was a thin 36 lots last Friday.
Bordeaux maize shaved 20 francs to 1,000 francs on spot delivery.
Sunny conditions in France's southwest are helping combining of early variety maize to make further headway, dealers said.
